Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically showing a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic pulmonary embolism. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, making severe right heart failure or massive cardiomegaly less likely than the vascular findings described in option B.
